questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: This high-power H&E section of myocardium shows haphazardly arranged, branching myofibers that lack the normal parallel orientation. This histologic hallmark is most characteristic of which condition?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Coagulative necrosis of acute myocardial infarction

explanation.summary: Disorganized, interwoven cardiomyocytes (myofiber disarray) with surrounding fibrosis are the microscopic signature of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and provide a substrate for arrhythmia and sudden death.
explanation.whyCorrect: Disorganized, interwoven cardiomyocytes (myofiber disarray) with surrounding fibrosis are the microscopic signature of hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and provide a substrate for arrhythmia and sudden death.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: This 12-lead ECG paired with a schematic of a thick-walled left ventricle shows tall R waves in the lateral leads and deep S waves in the right precordial leads. What do these voltage changes indicate?

explanation.summary: Increased LV muscle mass generates larger depolarization vectors, producing tall R waves laterally and deep S waves in V1-V2 that meet voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Increased LV muscle mass generates larger depolarization vectors, producing tall R waves laterally and deep S waves in V1-V2 that meet voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: These cardiac MRI images show a thickened myocardial segment (arrow) with a bright patchy area of late enhancement in the wall (star). In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, what does this bright region represent and why does it matter?

choices.label: B
choices.text: A perfusion artifact of no significance

choices.label: D
choices.text: Myocardial fibrosis, a marker of arrhythmic risk

explanation.summary: Late gadolinium enhancement reflects replacement fibrosis within hypertrophied myocardium; its extent correlates with ventricular arrhythmia and sudden-death risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.
explanation.whyCorrect: Late gadolinium enhancement reflects replacement fibrosis within hypertrophied myocardium; its extent correlates with ventricular arrhythmia and sudden-death risk in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: This four-chamber schematic contrasts a normal heart with HCM, emphasizing a disproportionately thick interventricular septum and small left ventricular cavity. What is this pattern called?

choices.label: E
choices.text: Eccentric dilatation of the left ventricle

explanation.summary: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy classically produces asymmetric hypertrophy that disproportionately thickens the interventricular septum relative to the free wall, reducing LV cavity size and predisposing to outflow obstruction.
explanation.whyCorrect: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy classically produces asymmetric hypertrophy that disproportionately thickens the interventricular septum relative to the free wall, reducing LV cavity size and predisposing to outflow obstruction.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: This gross cross-section of a heart shows marked, uniform thickening of the left ventricular free wall and interventricular septum with a small, slit-like chamber. This pattern of remodeling most commonly develops in response to which hemodynamic stress?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A high-output state such as chronic anemia

choices.label: C
choices.text: Infiltration of the myocardium by amyloid protein

choices.label: E
choices.text: Chronic volume overload from mitral regurgitation

explanation.summary: Uniform, concentric thickening of the LV wall with a reduced cavity size is the hallmark of concentric hypertrophy, which arises when the ventricle must generate sustained high pressures against an increased afterload (hypertension, aortic stenosis). Sarcomeres are laid down in parallel, thickening walls at the expense of chamber volume.
explanation.whyCorrect: Uniform, concentric thickening of the LV wall with a reduced cavity size is the hallmark of concentric hypertrophy, which arises when the ventricle must generate sustained high pressures against an increased afterload (hypertension, aortic stenosis). Sarcomeres are laid down in parallel, thickening walls at the expense of chamber volume.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: This diagram contrasts a normal heart with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, highlighting obstructed outflow and mitral regurgitation. Which mechanism links septal hypertrophy to both of these findings?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A ventricular septal defect shunting blood left-to-right

choices.label: B
choices.text: Rheumatic fusion of the mitral commissures

choices.label: C
choices.text: Systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve

choices.label: D
choices.text: Rupture of a papillary muscle after infarction

explanation.summary: In obstructive HCM the hypertrophied septum plus high-velocity outflow draws the anterior mitral leaflet toward the septum (systolic anterior motion), simultaneously obstructing the outflow tract and creating mitral regurgitation.
explanation.whyCorrect: In obstructive HCM the hypertrophied septum plus high-velocity outflow draws the anterior mitral leaflet toward the septum (systolic anterior motion), simultaneously obstructing the outflow tract and creating mitral regurgitation.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: This three-panel diagram shows a heart before surgery, during a procedure that incises the hypertrophied basal septum, and after surgery with increased outflow. What is the therapeutic goal of this operation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: To bypass an occluded coronary artery

choices.label: B
choices.text: To replace a stenotic aortic valve

choices.label: C
choices.text: To relieve left ventricular outflow tract obstruction

choices.label: D
choices.text: To ablate an accessory conduction pathway

choices.label: E
choices.text: To close an atrial septal defect

explanation.summary: Septal myomectomy removes part of the hypertrophied basal septum, widening the outflow tract, abolishing systolic anterior motion, and thereby relieving obstruction and associated mitral regurgitation in obstructive HCM.
explanation.whyCorrect: Septal myomectomy removes part of the hypertrophied basal septum, widening the outflow tract, abolishing systolic anterior motion, and thereby relieving obstruction and associated mitral regurgitation in obstructive HCM.

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: The diagram contrasts a normal ventricular cross-section with two remodeling patterns: one with a thick wall and small cavity, and one with a large cavity. Which stimulus produces the middle pattern (thick wall, reduced chamber volume)?

explanation.summary: Concentric hypertrophy (middle) results from pressure overload: increased systolic wall stress drives sarcomeres to be added in parallel, thickening the wall and reducing cavity volume. Eccentric hypertrophy (right, dilated) results instead from volume overload, with sarcomeres added in series.
explanation.whyCorrect: Concentric hypertrophy (middle) results from pressure overload: increased systolic wall stress drives sarcomeres to be added in parallel, thickening the wall and reducing cavity volume. Eccentric hypertrophy (right, dilated) results instead from volume overload, with sarcomeres added in series.

questions.imageRef: repic-764_Brick Exchange - Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy_p7_1.png

questions.topicName: Left Ventricular Hypertrophy and Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy
questions.stem: This figure shows a normal heart versus a thick-walled heart in which sarcomeres have been added in parallel within the myocytes. This structural change is the direct adaptive response to which condition?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Sustained pressure overload of the ventricle

choices.label: B
choices.text: Sustained volume overload of the ventricle

explanation.summary: Adding sarcomeres in parallel widens each myocyte and thickens the ventricular wall, producing concentric hypertrophy. This is the response to pressure overload (high afterload). Adding sarcomeres in series (lengthening) produces eccentric hypertrophy in response to volume overload.
explanation.whyCorrect: Adding sarcomeres in parallel widens each myocyte and thickens the ventricular wall, producing concentric hypertrophy. This is the response to pressure overload (high afterload). Adding sarcomeres in series (lengthening) produces eccentric hypertrophy in response to volume overload.
